glosses: to discuss over, to talk over (to discuss something thoroughly)
to discuss over, to talk over (to discuss for a certain period of time)
rozważyć wnikliwie podczas dyskusji
To talk too much.
To overcome or persuade by talking; talk over.
To overstate; overexaggerate; talk up to seem greater than what is actual.

examples.text: […] and he panted like a young faan in her fust race with the hounds, for he was overtalkin' his strength, and I feered he would die for sartin ef he didn't fetch up a bit and git rested; […]

glosses: Excessive talking.
Simultaneous speech or talk which drowns out all other speakers.
To discuss; to converse about a matter or issue.

examples.text: Come home early, we have a lot to talk over.
His reply was brief and to the point. "Come along to Doncaster," it read, "and we'll talk it over."

glosses: To persuade (someone); to talk around.

examples.text: I didn't like the idea at first, but they eventually talked me over.
She is an expert at talking others over to her views/side.

glosses: To verbally interrupt (someone); to speak at the same time as someone else.

examples.text: She rudely talked over her opponent in the debate.

glosses: To have each of a team's batting line-up positions complete an at-bat in the same half-inning.

examples.text: If the teams do not have the same number of players, the team with the greater number of players bats around once per inning, and the team with the smaller number of players will bat an equal number of times as the opposing team,[…].
[…]the Braves knocked Bunning out, batting around and scoring six runs in the fourth inning. They then scored four more runs the next inning, batting around once again against Dallas Green[…].

The Phillies thus batted around the lineup without a hit for the first time since July 17, 1992, a run that lasted more than 24 years, per ESPN Stats & Info. If not for the inning-ending double play, the Phillies might have even sent 10 or 11 batters to the plate without recording a single hit.

glosses: To have each of a team's batting line-up positions complete an at-bat in the same half-inning.
To have a team's first batter of the inning come to bat for a second time (after all of the others in the batting line-up have batted). (See the usage note below.)
To discuss.

examples.text: I think we've batted this idea around enough to take a decision.

glosses: To flit quickly from place to place.

examples.text: You must be tired after batting around all day.

glosses: To waste time; to idle or loaf.
To discuss or brainstorm (ideas) on a topic.

examples.text: We bounced around some suggestions in-house and then workshopped the best ones afterward.
We bounced some ideas around but didn't take it any further.

glosses: Synonym of jump around.
To switch between jobs, locations and other situations often.

examples.text: He was a grinder operator for years. He bounced around for a while because the small shops kept going under.

glosses: To tell (someone) step by step how to do something.

examples.text: The dispatcher will have to talk him through landing the plane in the middle of a hurricane!

glosses: To comfort someone as they endure trauma; to help someone consider an issue or see certain aspects of it.

examples.text: I'll talk him through the problem.
She's utterly grief-stricken, so I'm going over to talk her through it.
